expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: "For a few minutes old pods run against the new schema and every query touching legacy_email errors."

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: "The code change (stop reading the column) is fully reversible and safe to ship anytime. The DROP is the contract step and belongs in its own deploy."

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: "DROP COLUMN destroys the values... The restore path is a PITR/snapshot restore into a scratch DB plus a backfill join — hours, several people."

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: "Code-only revert: minutes, one person. Post-drop recovery: hours, multiple people, on a Saturday."

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: "Post-drop recovery: hours, multiple people, on a Saturday."

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: "Want me to write the CI guard that blocks a destructive ALTER/DROP from landing in the same PR as application code?"

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: "Short answer: merge the code half today, don't drop the column today."
